headline: Press minister, police spar over BNP leader's alleged arrest pressure
summary: A public dispute has erupted between the Bangladesh High Commission Press Minister in Delhi and Kushtia police over claims that a BNP leader was being pressured for arrest.
details: A Facebook post by Mustafizur Rahman Mustak, a BNP leader in Kushtia, expressing disillusionment with his party, triggered a public exchange between the press minister in Delhi and Kushtia district police.
The controversy began when Press Minister Saidur Rahman shared Mustak's post, claiming a powerful group was pressuring police to arrest Mustak at the behest of another BNP leader.
Kushtia district police rejected the allegation as "false" in a statement, asserting that neither the Khulna range DIG nor the district SP was aware of any such pressure.
Mustak told bdnews24.com that he feared for his safety and identified a local former MP as the person pressuring police to have him arrested.
Mustak further claimed that the SP had summoned him and told him to 'sort things out with that leader' or face arrest, though SP Aminul Islam has denied that any such conversation took place.
The dispute highlights internal tensions within the BNP, with Mustak claiming he was denied a fertilizer dealership and subsequently accused of sheltering extremists.
caption:
A public spat between a press minister and district police over the alleged arrest of a BNP leader has sparked controversy in Kushtia.

A Facebook post by Mustafizur Rahman Mustak, a BNP leader in Kushtia, expressing disillusionment with his party, triggered a public exchange between the press minister in Delhi and Kushtia district police.

The controversy began when Press Minister Saidur Rahman shared Mustak's post, claiming a powerful group was pressuring police to arrest Mustak at the behest of another BNP leader.

Kushtia district police rejected the allegation as "false" in a statement, asserting that neither the Khulna range DIG nor the district SP was aware of any such pressure.

Mustak told bdnews24.com that he feared for his safety and identified a local former MP as the person pressuring police to have him arrested.

Mustak further claimed that the SP had summoned him and told him to 'sort things out with that leader' or face arrest, though SP Aminul Islam has denied that any such conversation took place.

The dispute highlights internal tensions within the BNP, with Mustak claiming he was denied a fertilizer dealership and subsequently accused of sheltering extremists.

Source: bdnews24.com, Dhaka Tribune, Prothom Alo

headline_marked: ICT Division to launch [[‘One Citizen One ID’ system]] to unify digital footprints
headline: ICT Division to launch ‘One Citizen One ID’ system to unify digital footprints
summary: The initiative aims to merge NID, passport, and birth registration data to prevent fraud and misuse of information.
details: The ICT Division is taking steps to launch ‘One Citizen One ID’ to bring fragmented digital footprints under one umbrella. This move aims to unify databases such as NID, passports, birth registrations, and tax files to prevent the misuse of information and fraud.
caption:
Imagine one single ID for everything. Bangladesh is moving toward a ‘One Citizen One ID’ system to end data fragmentation and fraud.

The ICT Division is taking steps to launch ‘One Citizen One ID’ to bring fragmented digital footprints under one umbrella. This move aims to unify databases such as NID, passports, birth registrations, and tax files to prevent the misuse of information and fraud.
